target_customer: HR, people and operations teams at hybrid companies (and their employees)
problem: Hybrid teams did not know who was in the office when, relied on spreadsheets to coordinate, rarely met colleagues in person, and found internal events hard to organize.
business_model: B2B SaaS, freemium: free plan with unlimited seats and basic features; organization-wide rollout and advanced features paid (prices not found)
product_category: Hybrid-work scheduling and workplace engagement app

founders.name: Tom Nguyen
previous_startups: ASKIP (B2C mobile app, reportedly 6 million downloads without marketing, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he builds the company with his older brother.

founders.name: Arthur Lorotte de Banes
prior_employers: DevOps and cloud solutions architect roles (employers not named)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the company was founded by two brothers; the YC page names the two founders with different surnames, so which one is the brother is unclear.

investors: business angels (WeWork, Dropbox, GitHub, Snapchat, Intercom, Stripe, Alan, PayFit alumni)

competitors.name: Envoy
competitors.what: Workplace platform adding schedules, desk maps and 'sit nearby' features to see which coworkers are in the office

technical_complexity.rationale: A scheduling and status app with Slack, calendar and HR integrations is standard SaaS engineering; no hard technical problem is documented.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and organization-wide adoption create mild stickiness, but the features were copyable by workplace and collaboration vendors such as Envoy, and the free plan shows low willingness to pay.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Envoy shipped coworker schedules and desk-location features in August 2021, close to the YC batch; no source shows an acquisition or a shutdown of Café.

market_need_then: Before building, the founders said they interviewed 150 companies that all coordinated office attendance with spreadsheets (TechCrunch, 2021-05); the return-to-office and hybrid debate of 2021 created the need, and the first paying clients named were Livestorm, Jellysmack and Yubo.

branding.domain_note: Uses the domain-hack at.cafe (the .cafe TLD) rather than a .com; when and how acquired not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and social; features such as in-person 'Expresso Meetups' (per a search summary of the company's listings)

branding.brand_signature: The at.cafe domain and coffee-meetup theme
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch coverage in May 2021, a YC launch post and Product Hunt releases; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: A warm real-word name matched by a coffee-meetup metaphor and a memorable domain hack, but the word is a common noun that competes with coffee shops in search and there is no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Café started as a hybrid-office scheduling app that replaced spreadsheets, raised a $1M seed from 122West and Kima in May 2021 and joined YC Summer 2021, then broadened toward meeting colleagues in person and organizing events. It is still active with about ten people and a free plan, but there is no evidence of a later round, revenue scale or exit, and competitors such as Envoy added similar features at the time, so the outcome is a small surviving company whose growth is unproven.
notes: Seed $1M: TechCrunch (2021-05-28) and Nordic9 and Unleash agree on the amount; Nordic9 dates it January 2021, TechCrunch May 2021, so 2021-05 (the announcement date) is used. CB Insights (aggregator, unverified, not recorded) lists $1.5M over 3 rounds including a $0.5M convertible note on 2021-08-31 from Y Combinator. Founded 2020 per YC page. Envoy's article header says Aug 18, 2021 but its structured data says 2026, so the date is uncertain; TechCrunch named no direct competitors. Other tools in the category (Together, fikaTime, Impromptu) surfaced without 2021 dates and are excluded. Founders' education unknown. The at.cafe domain history and name origin not found.
